big: A REIT and an InvIT look alike on a screen: both are listed units that pay out income. But one earns from rent and the other from tolls and tariffs. Different engines, different risks.

lines: What is the same and what differs?

Same: a SEBI-regulated trust, listed units, at least 90% of NDCF paid out. Different: REITs hold rent-earning real estate, InvITs hold infrastructure. REIT income depends on occupancy and lease renewals, while InvIT income depends on traffic, tariffs and contract terms. From 1 January 2026, REITs count as equity-related for mutual funds. InvITs stay hybrid.
